contexts.text: The flame of a sword turning itself () = man's Own love with its insane cupidities and the derivative persuasions, which are such that he would fain enter, but is borne away from them to corporeal and earthly things. AC 309, Illustrated. ( = Divine truth in ultimates, which is like the Word in the sense of the letter, which can be thus turned. DSS 97:2.) ( = the terrific driving off and rejecting of all who are in falsities. AE 131:20.) ( = truth from the good of celestial love protecting. AE 277:3.)
Sword () = the punishment of falsities. AC 1188:3. AC 1296.
That the sword should be sent = a penalty of profanation.
Sword and famine () = to be bereaved of the Knowledges of truth and good... Sword = vastation as to spiritual things.
To fall by the mouth of the sword = by falsities; for a sword, in the Word, = the penalty for falsity.

Swords of stones () = the truths with which they were to be imbued in order that they might therewith chastise and dispel filthy loves; for there is never any purification without the Knowledges of truth. (See AC 2046:end.) AC 9659:2.
Sword = truth. AC 4135.

A sword (as distinguished from a knife) = truth combating... and also the vastation of truth; in the opposite, falsity combating, and the punishment of falsity. Fully illustrated. AC 3021:4. AC 3183:4. AC 3240:4. AC 3268:7. AC 3301:7. AC 5694:3.

By thy sword shalt thou live... () = that so long as truth is being conjoined with good, good will be apparently in the lower place; for a sword = truth combating... and the conjunction is effected by means of combats, that is, by means of temptations.
Sword = falsity combating against truth. AC 9050:9, References. AC 9164:end. AC 9182:6. AC 10227:9. AC 10406:7.
To kill the people with the sword () = to destroy truths by means of falsity.
The sword of Jehovah devoureth () = the devastation of truth.
A sword = truth combating and the consequent defence of truth; in the opposite, falsity combating and the consequent vastation of truth. AC 4728:2. AC 5044:6. AC 5044:9. AC 5120:8.
The reason a sword, here () = evil also, is that it was the sword of Levi... AC 4501.
I am not come to send peace, but a sword ()... = temptations; for a sword = truth combating; and, in the opposite, falsity combating. AE 131:2.
The sword, etc. = a state of desolation.
Sword = truth combating. AC 8617. AC 8813:end.
Thrust through with the sword = truth extinguished by falsity.
Lest He fall upon us with pestilence and the sword () = to avoid the damnation of evil and falsity.
In the Word four kinds of vastations and punishments are mentioned... and by the sword is signified the vastation of truth, and the punishment of falsity. Illustrated.
To put a sword in their hand to kill us () = that hence they have such ardour to destroy the truths of the Church by means of falsities. A sword = falsity combating and vastating.
A sword = truth combating, and destroying falsity; in the opposite, falsity combating, and destroying truth. AC 8294.
Sword = falsity.
I will draw out my sword () = the continual combat of falsity from evil.
Thy sword hath bereaved women () = that their falsity inflicts violence on the affections of good.
A drawn sword in his hand () = truth Divine combating in its power; for a sword = truth combating; and a drawn sword, combating continually against falsities and evils.
He hath delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh () = deliverance from the falsity of those who infested. A sword, in the opposite, = falsity combating and devastating.
To fall by the sword = to perish by falsity. References. AC 9014:5.
The sword = falsity combating and conquering.
The mouth of the sword () = truth combating and destroying the falsity which is from evil. AE 725:8.
I will slay you with the sword () = that they deprive themselves of good and truth through falsities.
Sword = falsity devastating the truth of faith. References.
Sword = truth combating against the falsity of evil. References.
Sword = truth combating against falsity. AC 9552:end.
Put ye everyone his sword upon his thigh () = truth from good combating against falsity from evil. Explained.
a [5]. To be devoured by the sword () = to perish by the falsity of evil.

Mention is often made in the Word of swords; and nothing else is signified by them than truth combating against falsities, and destroying them; and, in the opposite sense, falsity combating against truths; for by wars are signified spiritual wars... Illustrated. AR 836. AE 131.
The sword is upon the thigh, and therefore = combat from love; the sword is in the hand, and therefore = combat from power; and the sword is of the mouth, and therefore = combat from doctrine.
(Good Spirits who are interiorly Angels) have given them a sword with a silver hilt, together with a belt; and, when they carry that sword, the evil Spirits dare not do anything.

The angelic Societies with a Spirit inflow... also into the things which are external to his body... (as) is the case with those who have a sword, or even a staff with a cross-piece of wood, silver, or gold. This is done by influx from the Societies which are in the power of truth.
See Last Judgment. This is what is signified in the Word also by the flashing of a sword.
That a sword, in the Word, = 3 truth combating against falsity, and falsity against truth, and the consequent dispersion of falsities, and also spiritual temptation. Fully illustrated.

From all these passages it is evident what is signified by a sword in both senses. That such things are signified by a sword, is also from the appearances in the Spiritual World. When there are spiritual combats there, which are those of truth against falsity, and of falsity against truth, there then appear various war arms, as swords, spears, etc.; not because the combats are carried on with these, for they are only the representative appearances of spiritual combats. When falsities are combating sharply against truths, there sometimes appears from Heaven the brightness or flashing of a sword vibrating both ways, and causing great terror, by which those who are combating from falsities are dispersed. Illustrated.
The sword shall be upon... his right eye () = that all truth in the understanding will perish through falsity. AE 600:17.
They shall cut thee in pieces with swords () = that the Church will utterly die through falsifications of truth.
Gird Thy sword upon Thy thigh () = Divine truth combating from Divine good. AE 298:7.
The sword of Jehovah devoureth... () = falsity destroying truth. AE 314:8. AE 374:5. AE 730:8.
Neither shall the sword go through your land () = that falsity will not cast out truth. AE 365:14. AE 650:58.
The sword of Saul () = truth from good.
He hath given the nations... as the dust to His sword () = that the Lord disperses evils... as if they were nothing, by His Divine truth.
He hath made my mouth like a sharp sword () = that in the Lord and from Him is the Divine truth, by means of which falsities are dispersed.
God hath sharpened His sword ()... It is the evil man who sharpens the sword against himself... He sharpeneth the sword = that he acquires for himself falsity, by which he combats against truths.

In the Word mention is made of sword-gladius, short sword, and long sword, and by sword is signified this combat in general; by short sword, the combat of truth from good, or of falsity from evil; and by long sword, the combat of truth from doctrine against falsity, or of falsity from doctrine against truth; for a short sword is for the arm; and a long sword is said to go forth from the mouth.
Sword () = the deprivation of the Knowledges of truth, even until there is no more truth.
Sword = the deprivation of truth through falsities. AE 386:8, Illustrated. AE 388:20.
I will send a sword after them () = to destroy by the falsities of evil.
His words are softer than oil, yet are they drawn swords () = those who simulate good affections while they speak falsities by which they seduce... Drawn swords = falsities destroying.
The sword shall cut thee off () = that they will perish through falsities. AE 543:10.
Their tongue is a sharp sword () = crafty reasonings from falsities. These are called a sharp sword, because a sword = falsity destroying truth.
Those are said to be thrust through with the sword who have perished by falsities of evil. AE 659:20.
The direfulness and enormity of the falsity which destroys truth, is described by the sword made into lightning, and sharpened for slaughter ().
The sword shall be upon his arm () = falsity destroying every good of the will.
They shall fall by the mouth of the sword () = that they will perish through falsities. ( = the destruction of truth through falsities. AE 811.)
He shall slay the people with the sword () = that it will destroy truths through falsities.
The sword shall devour and be satiate, and shall be made drunk with their blood () = the total destruction of the natural man through falsities, and through the falsifications of truth.
The sword of a mighty man () = truth powerfully destroying falsity.

That by the consent of all, combats will then cease, is signified by they shall beat their swords into ploughshares... (; ); sword, and spear = falsities from evil combating against truths from good, and the converse.
They who are for the sword to the sword () = destruction through the derivative falsities.
To fall by the sword () = to perish through falsities.
My sword shall devour flesh () = that falsities will destroy all things of good.
All they that take the sword shall perish by the sword () = to receive the falsity of faith, and to perish by it.

He that hath no sword, let him sell his garments and buy one () = that those who have no truths must reject the things which are their Own, and procure for themselves truths with which to combat against falsities. A sword = the combat of truth against falsity, and the destruction of the latter.
My virgins and my young men have fallen by the sword () = that all the affection of truth and understanding of truth have perished through falsities.
Her priests have fallen by the sword () = that the goods of the Church, which are the goods of works, of charity, and of life, have been destroyed through falsities.
To be impoverished with the sword () = to be destroyed through falsities of evil.
